objective: Carry out Dow's statistical step on the field the CBFS inversion actually produced: fit the squared exponential covariance of the log discrepancy by maximum likelihood, and rule on whether that field is fit-able at all or is an artifact of an objective that cannot see it
rationale: The second of the three steps in Dow's structural-uncertainty method is a Gaussian random field fitted to the log discrepancy between the inferred and the modelled eddy viscosity, with a squared exponential covariance whose two parameters come from maximum likelihood. He reports the optimum for a straight channel and the correlation length he asserted for two-dimensional flows, and the whole step costs no solver time. This lab can run it today on machinery it already verified for a different purpose: the random matrix sampler carries a Nystrom solve of the covariance eigenproblem for an anisotropic squared exponential kernel, the truncated expansion, the interpolation from an auxiliary mesh to the mesh, and the field write path, and the whole chain was null tested by propagating an unperturbed field and recovering the baseline reattachment to one part in ten thousand. What is missing is a scalar variant of a tensor path and a two parameter likelihood maximisation, both arithmetic. The reason to run it now is not the fit but the diagnosis attached to it. The CBFS inversion plateaued at about 0.09 percent of its data term while its field moved substantially, reaching a multiplier of 0.735 in places, and the source method names exactly that combination: where the mean velocity gradient vanishes the objective is insensitive to the field, the sensitivity is identically zero there, and the field acquires structure the objective never sees, which does not spoil the velocity profile and does spoil any statistical model built on the field. Our objective carries a pull toward one and no smoothness term at all, so nothing in it addresses that null space. Fitting the covariance answers whether the moved cells sit where the adjoint has support or where it has none, and the same pass counts the cells where the stress limiter binds, which is where a multiplier on the omega equation cannot reach the eddy viscosity by the algebraic path. No solver runs and no flow case is started.
gate: Pre-registered before the fit is run: G1 the fitted process variance and correlation length are reported with the likelihood surface they came from, and with the nugget term the source method states, plus the check that shrinking the nugget does not move the optimum. G2 the moved cells are classified against the adjoint sensitivity support and against the limiter-active set, both counted, and the two overlaps stated as fractions. G3 the verdict is one of fit-able, fit-able only outside the objective's null space, or not fit-able, and it is stated before any propagation is proposed. A fitted correlation length at the mesh scale is reported as evidence of a field with no spatial structure, never as a correlation length
cost_basis: estimate, and the estimate is that no solver runs. The eigenproblem is dense and symmetric on a coarse auxiliary mesh; the earlier study used a fifty by thirty auxiliary mesh with thirty retained modes capturing 98.95 percent of the variance, and solved it in seconds. Every input field is already written to disk by runs that have been paid for
expected_knowledge_gain: Each outcome changes a decision. A covariance with a physically sensible correlation length, fitted on cells the adjoint can see, means the statistical step works here and the band program proceeds to propagation. A field whose structure sits in the objective's null space convicts the missing smoothness term rather than the method, and makes adding it a precondition on any future inversion run for an uncertainty purpose, at no solver cost per evaluation because its sensitivity is computed directly rather than through the adjoint. A field with no spatial structure at all says the inversion produced nothing to model and stops the band program before core-minutes are spent on sampling it. The limiter overlap count is a number nobody has, and it is the cheapest available test of the parameterization hypothesis behind the plateau
